templates_considered: no_secrets_in_code (SEC-012): fits; the ask is 'no hardcoded keys' and it is the template for exactly that
approved_vendors_only (VND-001): did not fit; the ask is about literal credentials, not destinations
protect_card_data recipe: not used; it also contains no_secrets_in_code but covers card data the customer did not ask about

rules.covers: API keys/tokens written as literals in functions and endpoints (e.g. the pasted Twilio key). Default patterns (all) and default locations (definition, agent_settings). env deliberately not scanned, since env is where the secret belongs.

ask_parts_not_covered.part: Passwords hardcoded in a function or endpoint (generic string literals, not key-shaped)
Confirming that the Twilio key the contractor pasted is gone from the workspace and rotated
ask_parts_not_covered.why: needs runtime/org process (rotation is outside definitions); presence is only visible after evaluation, which I was not allowed to run

ask_parts_not_covered.part: Requirement that secrets 'come from environment variables' as a positive rule (every secret must be an $env reference)
ask_parts_not_covered.why: couldn't tell how: literal.credential_shape only forbids recognisable literals; no check requires a value to come from $env

assumptions: The customer wants a blocking-free, advisory policy by default; the template's critical severity kept
'Twilio key' is matched by the twilio pattern, which the catalogue describes as matching identifiers rather than secrets; I assumed it is useful for the customer's case anyway
Tags soc2 and pci_dss taken from the template's frameworks list; no workspace tag check was run, so these are metadata only
Policy key SEC-012 reused from the template; no other policy key exists in the workspace (xano policy list returned none)
confusions: The skill says to pull the workspace and read endpoints/functions before writing, but this rule names no tables, tags or API groups, so the pull gave nothing I needed; the brief also restricts evaluate, so I could not confirm whether the rule matches anything today.

The skill's 'params' note says to omit params when the check needs nothing; the template's Fill column says 'nothing', so I wrote params = {} and the parser dropped it on output. Fine, but worth documenting that both forms are equivalent.

Catalogue description says aws and twilio 'match identifiers rather than secrets', which sits awkwardly with the customer's Twilio key case: it is unclear whether a pasted Twilio API key would be reported or only a Twilio account identifier.

The check's description says it reports 'secrets written as literal values'; it is unclear how it treats a password string literal assigned to a variable named password. No example in the catalogue covers that case.
wished_for: A way to express 'secrets come from $env' as a positive requirement, or a catalogue entry naming which literal patterns (passwords, bearer tokens in headers) are covered
A worked example of literal.credential_shape flagging a Twilio key, with the exact pattern id that fires
A note in the template table on whether the template's rule set includes generic password literals
why_confidence: The check reliably catches recognisable key formats (including Twilio, per the catalogue) in definitions. It does not catch generic passwords, and the rule was not evaluated against the workspace, so I cannot say it would fire on the contractor's actual code.
